candidate_sources.title: Cercospora Leaf Spot and Berry Blotch of Coffee
candidate_sources.snippet: University of Hawaii CTAHR extension factsheet PD-41 covering Cercospora coffeicola on coffee. Describes leaf spot and berry blotch symptoms, pathogen biology, environmental conditions favoring disease, and management recommendations including cultural and chemical controls.

candidate_sources.title: Cercospora coffeicola; Brown eye spot, Berry blotch - Plantwise Knowledge Bank
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Plantwise datasheet on Cercospora coffeicola covering brown eye spot and berry blotch of coffee. Includes symptoms on leaves and berries, pathogen identity, geographic distribution, host range, diagnosis, and integrated pest management. Berry blotch characterized by dark-brown blotchy lesions with yellow to red halo.

candidate_sources.title: Cercospora Leaf Spot and Berry Blotch - Hawaii Coffee Education
candidate_sources.snippet: Hawaii coffee grower education page on Cercospora leaf spot and berry blotch caused by Cercospora coffeicola. Covers symptoms on leaves and berries, disease cycle, favorable conditions (20-28°C, 36-72 hours wetness), and management strategies including pruning, nutrition, and fungicide options.

candidate_sources.title: Black rot or koleroga - TNAU Agritech Portal
candidate_sources.snippet: Black rot or koleroga of coffee caused by Koleroga noxia. The pathogen infects leaves, developing berries and young shoots. Infected leaves get detached from branches and remain hanging within slimy fungal strands.

candidate_sources.title: Understanding and Managing Black Rot Disease in Coffee - Agriculture Notes
candidate_sources.snippet: Black rot disease is caused by the fungus Koleroga noxia and primarily targets coffee plants in regions with high humidity and excessive rainfall. Young shoots and tender stem portions turn completely black within days of infection. The disease attacks leaves, branches, twigs and berries with characteristic blight symptoms.

candidate_sources.title: Management of coffee black rot disease caused by Koleroga Noxia Donk
candidate_sources.snippet: Black rot can cause crop losses of up to 30%. Cultural practices like thinning shade, avoiding monoculture of shade trees, and training coffee bushes reduce pathogen inoculum. Continuous use of conventional fungicides like carbendazim has led to resistance development.

candidate_sources.title: Fact sheet - Coffee brown-eye spot (142) - Pacific Pests, Pathogens, Weeds & Pesticides
candidate_sources.snippet: Detailed fact sheet covering symptoms on leaves (light brown/grey centres with dark brown ring and yellow margin, up to 15mm), berries (brown irregular to oval spots causing premature ripening), nursery impacts (leaf fall, stem dieback). Pathogen: Cercospora coffeicola (sexual form Mycosphaerella coffeicola). Cultural and chemical management including spacing, N/K nutrition, shade (35-65%), copper protectants and triazole systemics.

candidate_sources.title: Mycosphaerella coffeicola (brown eye spot of coffee) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet on Mycosphaerella coffeicola (anamorph Cercospora coffeicola), the causal agent of brown eye spot of coffee. Covers distribution, biology, symptoms, hosts, and control measures.

candidate_sources.title: Perileucoptera coffeella (coffee leaf miner) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI datasheet covering identity, distribution, hosts, diagnosis, biology & ecology, natural enemies, impacts, and prevention/control. Coffee leaves infested with P. coffeella are recognized by the presence of large, irregular, brown spots on the upper surface of the leaf. Larvae feed on the palisade parenchyma causing necrosis, defoliation, and significant yield loss.

candidate_sources.title: Coffee Leaf Miner | Pests & Diseases - Plantix
candidate_sources.snippet: Detailed pest profile covering symptoms, trigger conditions, and management. Symptoms include pale yellow trails under leaf epidermis, large necrotic patches, and brown papery spots. Larvae create mines in the mesophyll causing necrosis and reducing photosynthetic leaf surface. Several larvae on one leaf can cause necrosis of up to 90% of its structure.

candidate_sources.title: A Comprehensive Review of the Coffee Leaf Miner Leucoptera coffeella (Lepidoptera: Lyonetiidae) — A Major Pest for the Coffee Crop in Brazil and Others Neotropical Countries
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive peer-reviewed review covering biology, ecology, damage assessment, natural enemies, chemical control, biological control, resistant cultivars, and integrated pest management. Losses range from 30–70%, with defoliation up to 75%. Threshold of four mines per leaf before shedding. Covers both Leucoptera coffeella (Latin America) and Leucoptera caffeina (Africa).

candidate_sources.title: Phoma | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet covering Phoma identity, distribution, hosts/species affected, diagnosis, biology and ecology, and further information for this fungal plant pathogen genus affecting coffee and other crops.

candidate_sources.title: Phoma diseases: Epidemiology and control - Deb - 2020 - Plant Pathology - Wiley Online Library
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive review of Phoma diseases covering epidemiology and control strategies. Discusses Phoma spp. as pathogens on multiple crops including coffee, with details on infection biology, environmental conditions favoring disease (15-20°C, leaf wetness), and management approaches.

candidate_sources.title: Phoma costaricensis - Wikipedia
candidate_sources.snippet: Phoma costaricensis is a plant pathogen infecting coffee. It is a soil fungus that infects the leaves and fruits of the coffee plant prior to the fruit ripening, causing leaf lesions, drying of branches, and rotting of flowers and fruits.

candidate_sources.title: Coffee Leaf Rust - North Central Integrated Pest Management Center
candidate_sources.snippet: Coffee leaf rust caused by Hemileia vastatrix is a devastating foliar disease. Symptoms include yellowish oily spots on upper leaf surface expanding into larger round spots turning bright orange to red. Management strategies include fungicide programs, cultural practices, and resistant varieties.

candidate_sources.title: Coffee leaf rust: Hemileia vastatrix - CABI Plantwise Plus Knowledge Bank
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive datasheet on Hemileia vastatrix covering identity, distribution, hosts, symptoms, biology, detection, management and economic impact of coffee leaf rust worldwide.

candidate_sources.title: Spraying to Suppress Coffee Leaf Rust (Hemileia vastatrix) - University of Hawaii CTAHR
candidate_sources.snippet: University of Hawaii extension publication on coffee leaf rust management. Covers disease cycle, symptoms identification, and fungicide spray programs for suppression of Hemileia vastatrix in Hawaiian coffee production.
